positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): The rightly guided caliphs prayed with Arabic Qur’an, so their practice binds believers under commands to follow Abu Bakr and Umar and the caliphs’ Sunna.

positions.position: A Prophetic report calls the basmala the key to every book.
positions.reasons: DURR (محمد بن علي): A Prophetic report calls the basmala the key to every book.

positions.position: A Prophetic report from Yazid ibn Thabit instructs scribes to make the sin clear in the basmala.
positions.reasons: DURR (يزيد بن ثابت): A Prophetic report from Yazid ibn Thabit instructs scribes to make the sin clear in the basmala.

positions.position: Muslim ibn Yasar disliked beginning the basmala in abbreviated form as bm, omitting the sin.
positions.reasons: DURR (مسلم بن يسار): Muslim ibn Yasar disliked beginning the basmala in abbreviated form as bm, omitting the sin.

positions.position: In a very weak report, Jesus explains the letters of the basmala: ba is God's majesty, sin His splendor, mim His dominion, and the names describe divine lordship and mercy.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (عيسى): In a very weak report, Jesus explains the letters of the basmala: ba is God's majesty, sin His splendor, mim His dominion, and the names describe divine lordship and mercy.

positions.position: A report attributed to the Prophet instructs scribes not to extend the ba to the mim before raising the sin.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): A report attributed to the Prophet instructs scribes not to extend the ba to the mim before raising the sin.

positions.position: A report attributed to the Prophet tells scribes to make the sin distinct in the basmala.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (يزيد بن ثابت): A report attributed to the Prophet tells scribes to make the sin distinct in the basmala.

question: What inward meanings are drawn from the basmala?

positions.position: Before beginning the ascent, the worshipper purifies body and clothing for the holy presence and chooses which of opposing companions—angel or devil, reason or desire, truth or falsehood, and so forth—to follow, since settled companionship is hard to break.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Before beginning the ascent, the worshipper purifies body and clothing for the holy presence and chooses which of opposing companions—angel or devil, reason or desire, truth or falsehood, and so forth—to follow, since settled companionship is hard to break. | mentions 9:119

positions.position: He links the basmala’s bāʾ to Muḥammad’s merciful reality and cites 21:107 and 9:128; the basmala’s opening then signals the Prophet’s mercy and mission.
positions.reasons: ALUSI (author): He links the basmala’s bāʾ to Muḥammad’s merciful reality and cites 21:107 and 9:128; the basmala’s opening then signals the Prophet’s mercy and mission. | mentions 21:107, 9:128

positions.position: He associates the missing basmala in al-Tawba with that sūra’s manifest severity, while claiming a concealed allusion to the Prophetic reality remains.
positions.reasons: ALUSI (author): He associates the missing basmala in al-Tawba with that sūra’s manifest severity, while claiming a concealed allusion to the Prophetic reality remains.

positions.position: Alusi links the basmala's ba to the Muhammadan reality and first determination, saying divine effusion came through the Prophet and citing reports that his light was created first and the cosmos for his sake.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): Alusi links the basmala's ba to the Muhammadan reality and first determination, saying divine effusion came through the Prophet and citing reports that his light was created first and the cosmos for his sake.

question: How does the basmala connect with its sūra or other verses?

positions.position: Ibn ʿUmar says the basmala was revealed in every sūra.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (ابن عمر): Ibn ʿUmar says the basmala was revealed in every sūra. DURR (ابن عمر): Ibn Umar says the basmala was revealed in every sura. DURR-FULL (ابن عمر): Ibn Umar says the basmala was revealed in every surah.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says Muslims knew a sura had ended when the basmala was revealed; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
positions.reasons: DURR (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Muslims knew a sura had ended when the basmala was revealed; al-Hakim authenticated the report. ITQAN (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Muslims knew a sūra had ended when the basmala descended; al-Hakim’s chain meets the standards of the two Sahih collections.

positions.position: Ibn Umar says the Prophet recited the basmala in al-Fatiha and the following sura.
positions.reasons: DURR (ابن عمر): Ibn Umar says the Prophet recited the basmala in al-Fatiha and the following sura. DURR-FULL (نافع): Nafi reports Ibn Umar's practice of reciting the basmala in al-Fatiha and the following surah, which Ibn Umar traced to hearing the Prophet.

positions.position: All agree the basmala is Qur’an in sura 27, but disagree whether it belongs in the Fatiha and at the opening of every sura.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (author): All agree the basmala is Qur’an in sura 27, but disagree whether it belongs in the Fatiha and at the opening of every sura.

positions.position: Muḥammad holds that the basmala is recited before each sūra.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (محمد): Muḥammad holds that the basmala is recited before each sūra.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet knew a surah had ended when the basmala descended.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says the Prophet knew a surah had ended when the basmala descended.

positions.position: Ibn Masud says the community learned where one surah ended and another began when the basmala was revealed.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI-FULL (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masud says the community learned where one surah ended and another began when the basmala was revealed.

positions.position: An authentic report has the Prophet ask Ubayy to recite the surah; Ubayy begins with al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin and continues to its end, without the basmala.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA (أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): An authentic report has the Prophet ask Ubayy to recite the surah; Ubayy begins with al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin and continues to its end, without the basmala.

positions.position: The Jabir and Abu Hurayra reports can be reconciled as instructional recitations rather than proof that the basmala belongs to the sura.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (author): The Jabir and Abu Hurayra reports can be reconciled as instructional recitations rather than proof that the basmala belongs to the sura.

positions.position: The Prophet omitted the basmala when teaching Ubay because he was identifying the sura's contents, whereas that aim was absent in the other two reports.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (author): The Prophet omitted the basmala when teaching Ubay because he was identifying the sura's contents, whereas that aim was absent in the other two reports.

positions.position: Al-Shafi‘i prefers repeating the basmala before every sura, citing the report that an important matter begun without it is cut off.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (الشافعي): Al-Shafi‘i prefers repeating the basmala before every sura, citing the report that an important matter begun without it is cut off.

positions.position: Razi’s school holds that a menstruating woman or a person in major ritual impurity may not recite the basmala.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Razi’s school holds that a menstruating woman or a person in major ritual impurity may not recite the basmala.

positions.position: Qurṭubī calls the basmala a divine pledge at every sūra’s head, affirming its truth and God’s fulfillment of promises.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Qurṭubī calls the basmala a divine pledge at every sūra’s head, affirming its truth and God’s fulfillment of promises.

positions.position: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq calls the basmala crowns of the sūras; Qurṭubī takes this to suggest it separates sūras, not that it forms their verses.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (جعفر الصادق): Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq calls the basmala crowns of the sūras; Qurṭubī takes this to suggest it separates sūras, not that it forms their verses.

positions.position: Qurṭubī reads the report as three opening verses for God, one shared verse, and three for the servant; “Anʿamta ʿalayhim” is a verse.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Qurṭubī reads the report as three opening verses for God, one shared verse, and three for the servant; “Anʿamta ʿalayhim” is a verse.

positions.position: The Companions reportedly knew a sūra had ended when the basmala was revealed; al-Ḥasan says it appeared in letters and only in al-Naml as Qurʾān.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (الصحابة): The Companions reportedly knew a sūra had ended when the basmala was revealed; al-Ḥasan says it appeared in letters and only in al-Naml as Qurʾān. | mentions 27:30

positions.position: Qurṭubī rejects reasoning as proof of Qurʾānic text and notes uncertainty about the basmala at each sūra.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Qurṭubī rejects reasoning as proof of Qurʾānic text and notes uncertainty about the basmala at each sūra.

positions.position: Abū Ḥanīfa gave no explicit ruling here; Bayḍāwī infers that he considered the basmala outside the sūra.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI (أبو حنيفة): Abū Ḥanīfa gave no explicit ruling here; Bayḍāwī infers that he considered the basmala outside the sūra.

positions.position: The basmala and following words through the sura are placed on the servants' tongues to teach invocation, praise, and asking for grace.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): The basmala and following words through the sura are placed on the servants' tongues to teach invocation, praise, and asking for grace.

positions.position: A sound Abu Dawud report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet recognized a surah's division when the basmala was revealed; it is also reported mursal from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): A sound Abu Dawud report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet recognized a surah's division when the basmala was revealed; it is also reported mursal from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.

positions.position: The basmala is counted in readings where it descended with the sūra and omitted in readings where it did not.
positions.reasons: BURHAN (author): The basmala is counted in readings where it descended with the sūra and omitted in readings where it did not.

positions.position: After reaching Saba in his tenth year of writing, Biqāʿī concluded that each sūra's name gives a general indication of its purpose; that purpose guides the sūra's coherence.
positions.reasons: BIQAI (author): After reaching Saba in his tenth year of writing, Biqāʿī concluded that each sūra's name gives a general indication of its purpose; that purpose guides the sūra's coherence.

positions.position: Biqāʿī states each sūra's purpose, aligns it with its name, and explains its basmala in a way suited to that purpose without leaving the words' meanings.
positions.reasons: BIQAI (author): Biqāʿī states each sūra's purpose, aligns it with its name, and explains its basmala in a way suited to that purpose without leaving the words' meanings.

positions.position: Ibn Masud says the basmala shields a reader from each of Hell's nineteen guardians.
positions.reasons: DURR (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masud says the basmala shields a reader from each of Hell's nineteen guardians.

positions.position: A sound-chain report says every important affair not begun with the basmala is cut off or deficient.
positions.reasons: DURR (النبي): A sound-chain report says every important affair not begun with the basmala is cut off or deficient.

positions.position: Yahya ibn Atiq says al-Hasan directed scribes to place the basmala at the imam's opening and draw a line between pairs of suras.
positions.reasons: DURR (الحسن): Yahya ibn Atiq says al-Hasan directed scribes to place the basmala at the imam's opening and draw a line between pairs of suras.

positions.position: A good-chain report calls al-Fatiha the best sura revealed and says it contains healing for every illness.
positions.reasons: DURR (عبد الله بن جابر): A good-chain report calls al-Fatiha the best sura revealed and says it contains healing for every illness.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel's recitation of the basmala signaled that a sura was being given.
positions.reasons: DURR (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Gabriel's recitation of the basmala signaled that a sura was being given.

positions.position: The Prophet did not know where one surah ended until the basmala came; another wording says he then knew the next surah had begun.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): The Prophet did not know where one surah ended until the basmala came; another wording says he then knew the next surah had begun.

positions.position: Muslims recognized a surah's ending when the basmala was revealed.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): Muslims recognized a surah's ending when the basmala was revealed.

positions.position: In the Prophet's time, revelation of the basmala signaled that one surah had ended and another had come down.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (سعيد بن جبير): In the Prophet's time, revelation of the basmala signaled that one surah had ended and another had come down.

positions.position: When Gabriel recited the basmala to the Prophet, he knew it was a surah.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): When Gabriel recited the basmala to the Prophet, he knew it was a surah.

positions.position: Ibn Masud says people did not know the boundary between surahs until the basmala was revealed.
positions.reasons: DURR-FULL (ابن مسعود): Ibn Masud says people did not know the boundary between surahs until the basmala was revealed.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet learned a sūra’s boundary when the basmala was revealed; al-Bazzar adds that it marked a completed sūra and the next one.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet learned a sūra’s boundary when the basmala was revealed; al-Bazzar adds that it marked a completed sūra and the next one.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas reports that when Gabriel recited the basmala, the Prophet knew it was a sūra; al-Hakim grades the chain sound.
positions.reasons: ITQAN (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): Ibn Abbas reports that when Gabriel recited the basmala, the Prophet knew it was a sūra; al-Hakim grades the chain sound.

positions.position: He defines a sūra as Qurʾān containing an opening and a conclusion; another definition, an independent portion, distinguishes named units such as Āyat al-Kursī.
positions.reasons: ALUSI (author): He defines a sūra as Qurʾān containing an opening and a conclusion; another definition, an independent portion, distinguishes named units such as Āyat al-Kursī.

positions.position: Dividing the Qurʾān into sūras energizes readers, makes each memorized unit feel complete, and establishes each sūra as an independent sign and miracle.
positions.reasons: ALUSI (author): Dividing the Qurʾān into sūras energizes readers, makes each memorized unit feel complete, and establishes each sūra as an independent sign and miracle.

positions.position: Alusi allows that Ibn Abbas may have based the identification on Prophetic instruction as he understood it, without thereby asserting the basmala is a portion of the sura.
positions.reasons: ALUSI-FULL (author): Alusi allows that Ibn Abbas may have based the identification on Prophetic instruction as he understood it, without thereby asserting the basmala is a portion of the sura.

positions.position: The dispute concerns whether Qur’anic status recurs at sura openings, not whether the basmala is Qur’an at all; Ibn Rushd al-Ḥafīd makes this distinction.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR (author): The dispute concerns whether Qur’anic status recurs at sura openings, not whether the basmala is Qur’an at all; Ibn Rushd al-Ḥafīd makes this distinction.

positions.position: Readers who do not count it as a verse may recite it at a sura opening as a recommended act of blessing that imitates the muṣḥaf scribes; this practice does not prove their legal position.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR (author): Readers who do not count it as a verse may recite it at a sura opening as a recommended act of blessing that imitates the muṣḥaf scribes; this practice does not prove their legal position.

positions.position: Whether the basmala at a given sura opening must be recited depends instead on transmitted recitation and sound Sunna reports.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (author): Whether the basmala at a given sura opening must be recited depends instead on transmitted recitation and sound Sunna reports.

positions.position: Abd al-Hakim treats sura names and Meccan or Medinan labels in the codex as later additions, assuming the Companions did not write them.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (عبد الحكيم): Abd al-Hakim treats sura names and Meccan or Medinan labels in the codex as later additions, assuming the Companions did not write them.

positions.position: If some early authorities wrote those labels, as al-Qastallani and other scholars suggest, later copyists' basmala evidence fails; the claim that labels used different ink is contradicted by old one-color codices.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (author): If some early authorities wrote those labels, as al-Qastallani and other scholars suggest, later copyists' basmala evidence fails; the claim that labels used different ink is contradicted by old one-color codices.

positions.position: A Bukhari report says Anas demonstrated the Prophet's measured reading by stretching the basmala, but Ibn Ashur says the pronouns refer to Anas, who merely used the familiar formula as an example.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (أنس): A Bukhari report says Anas demonstrated the Prophet's measured reading by stretching the basmala, but Ibn Ashur says the pronouns refer to Anas, who merely used the familiar formula as an example.

positions.position: A Muslim report from Anas says the Prophet announced a newly revealed sura and recited the basmala before al-Kawthar; Ibn al-Mubarak and a second Shafi'i position cite it for the basmala.
positions.reasons: IBNASHUR-FULL (أنس): A Muslim report from Anas says the Prophet announced a newly revealed sura and recited the basmala before al-Kawthar; Ibn al-Mubarak and a second Shafi'i position cite it for the basmala. | mentions 108:1

positions.position: Al-Sadiq condemns those who called the greatest verse an innovation when recited aloud; al-Baqir says they stole the Qur'an's noblest verse and urges beginning every affair with it for blessing.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (الصادق): Al-Sadiq condemns those who called the greatest verse an innovation when recited aloud; al-Baqir says they stole the Qur'an's noblest verse and urges beginning every affair with it for blessing.

positions.position: Anas reports the Prophet reciting the basmala when a sura was newly revealed; Ibn Abbas reports that it marked the boundary between suras, and the author notes corroboration from al-Baqir.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (النبي): Anas reports the Prophet reciting the basmala when a sura was newly revealed; Ibn Abbas reports that it marked the boundary between suras, and the author notes corroboration from al-Baqir.

positions.position: The basmala in each sura is tied to that sura's distinct purpose; here the purpose is worshipful praise, so the basmala begins that act of servitude.
positions.reasons: TABATABAI (author): The basmala in each sura is tied to that sura's distinct purpose; here the purpose is worshipful praise, so the basmala begins that act of servitude.

positions.position: Most authorities count the opening invocation as verse 1 of Al-Fatihah; in other surahs it precedes the text without being counted.
positions.reasons: ASAD-NOTES (author): Most authorities count the opening invocation as verse 1 of Al-Fatihah; in other surahs it precedes the text without being counted. | mentions 9:1

positions.position: Shafi‘i counts the Fatiha basmala as one of its verses; two views are reported for other surahs, with inclusion in each surah recorded as the more sound report from him.
positions.reasons: KURANYOLU-TEFSIR (İmam Şâfiî): Shafi‘i counts the Fatiha basmala as one of its verses; two views are reported for other surahs, with inclusion in each surah recorded as the more sound report from him.

positions.position: A saying attributed to ʿAlī compresses the Quran into the Fātiḥah, the basmalah, its opening bāʾ, and the diacritical point beneath it.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib): A saying attributed to ʿAlī compresses the Quran into the Fātiḥah, the basmalah, its opening bāʾ, and the diacritical point beneath it.

positions.position: The point beneath bāʾ can symbolize the Divine Pen’s first drop of ink, which inscribed all archetypes on the Preserved Tablet before creation; thus basmalah marks both Quranic and cosmic beginnings.
positions.reasons: STUDYQURAN (author): The point beneath bāʾ can symbolize the Divine Pen’s first drop of ink, which inscribed all archetypes on the Preserved Tablet before creation; thus basmalah marks both Quranic and cosmic beginnings. | mentions 68:1, 96:4, 85:22

question: How does seeking refuge relate to this opening?

positions.position: Ibn Abbas says Satan caused people to overlook the basmala.
positions.reasons: DURR (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Satan caused people to overlook the basmala. DURR-FULL (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says Satan caused people to overlook the basmala.

positions.position: Seeking refuge means seeking protection or asylum.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Seeking refuge means seeking protection or asylum.

positions.position: Refuge formula asks God alone to protect from Satan harming religion or diverting from duty owed the Lord.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Refuge formula asks God alone to protect from Satan harming religion or diverting from duty owed the Lord.

positions.position: Satan can mean any rebellious being among jinn, humans, animals or other things; Qurʾān speaks of human and jinn satans; 6:112.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Satan can mean any rebellious being among jinn, humans, animals or other things; Qurʾān speaks of human and jinn satans; 6:112.

positions.position: A bucking barẕawn kept prancing despite Umar’s blows; he dismounted and called it a satan.
positions.reasons: TAB (عمر بن الخطاب): A bucking barẕawn kept prancing despite Umar’s blows; he dismounted and called it a satan.

positions.position: A rebel is called satan for departing from its kind and from good; another derivation links word to being distant.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): A rebel is called satan for departing from its kind and from good; another derivation links word to being distant.

positions.position: Al-Nābigha’s shatūn means distant, supporting Satan from shatana.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Al-Nābigha’s shatūn means distant, supporting Satan from shatana.

positions.position: Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s shāṭin supports shatana yashṭunu; if from shāṭa yashīṭ the form would be shāʾiṭ.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s shāṭin supports shatana yashṭunu; if from shāṭa yashīṭ the form would be shāʾiṭ.

positions.position: Rajīm is a passive faʿīl meaning accursed or reviled; stoning may be verbal abuse or physical throwing.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Rajīm is a passive faʿīl meaning accursed or reviled; stoning may be verbal abuse or physical throwing.

positions.position: Abraham's father uses stone you as a verbal threat, illustrating rajm by speech; 19:46.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Abraham's father uses stone you as a verbal threat, illustrating rajm by speech; 19:46.

positions.position: Satan may be called stoned because God expelled him from heaven and pelted him with meteors.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Satan may be called stoned because God expelled him from heaven and pelted him with meteors.

positions.position: Ibn Abbas reports Gabriel first taught Muhammad to seek refuge, then say basmala, then recite 96:1; he calls this first sūra revealed through Gabriel.
positions.reasons: TAB (عبد الله بن عباس): Ibn Abbas reports Gabriel first taught Muhammad to seek refuge, then say basmala, then recite 96:1; he calls this first sūra revealed through Gabriel.

positions.position: In Ibn ʿAbbās’s report, Gabriel glosses the basmala as reading, standing, and sitting in remembrance of God.
positions.reasons: TAB (عبد الله بن عباس): In Ibn ʿAbbās’s report, Gabriel glosses the basmala as reading, standing, and sitting in remembrance of God.

positions.position: Ḥumayd ibn Thawr’s verse calls fifty one’s “mother” because it encompasses all numbers below it.
positions.reasons: TAB (author): Ḥumayd ibn Thawr’s verse calls fifty one’s “mother” because it encompasses all numbers below it.

positions.position: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Gabriel first taught seeking refuge and then instructed Muhammad to read, rise, and sit in remembrance of his Lord.
positions.reasons: TAB-FULL (عبد الله بن عباس): Ibn ʿAbbās reports Gabriel first taught seeking refuge and then instructed Muhammad to read, rise, and sit in remembrance of his Lord.

positions.position: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Daḥḥāk derive ilāh from seeking refuge and relying on someone: creatures turn to God in crises, and He protects them.
positions.reasons: THALABI (ابن عباس والضحاك): Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Daḥḥāk derive ilāh from seeking refuge and relying on someone: creatures turn to God in crises, and He protects them.

positions.position: Al-Mubarrad derives it from finding repose with someone; creatures become calm through remembrance of God.
positions.reasons: THALABI (المبرد): Al-Mubarrad derives it from finding repose with someone; creatures become calm through remembrance of God. | mentions 13:28

positions.position: Al-Qannād derives it from walāh, loss of reason at losing a beloved; the author says hearts long for God in love and tremble at His remembrance.
positions.reasons: THALABI (علي بن عبد الرحيم القناد): Al-Qannād derives it from walāh, loss of reason at losing a beloved; the author says hearts long for God in love and tremble at His remembrance.

positions.position: The Qur’an and Sunna establish that a reciter seeks refuge before reciting, saying I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (author): The Qur’an and Sunna establish that a reciter seeks refuge before reciting, saying I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed.

positions.position: Alternatively, al-rajim means one who is pelted, specifically with stars.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): Alternatively, al-rajim means one who is pelted, specifically with stars.

positions.position: Another explanation of one who is pelted is that he is ill-omened.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): Another explanation of one who is pelted is that he is ill-omened.

positions.position: A third explanation is that al-rajim means accursed, that is, expelled.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): A third explanation is that al-rajim means accursed, that is, expelled.

positions.position: In the Prophetic formula, Satan’s puff means pride, his spittle means magic, and his provocation means madness.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (author): In the Prophetic formula, Satan’s puff means pride, his spittle means magic, and his provocation means madness.

positions.position: Abu Sa‘id reports that the Prophet also sought refuge in God the All-Hearing, All-Knowing from Satan’s puff, spittle, and provocation; no grading is stated.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (أبو سعيد الخدري): Abu Sa‘id reports that the Prophet also sought refuge in God the All-Hearing, All-Knowing from Satan’s puff, spittle, and provocation; no grading is stated.

positions.position: One explanation takes seeking refuge as seeking protection from one possessing power.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): One explanation takes seeking refuge as seeking protection from one possessing power.

positions.position: Another explanation takes it as humbly seeking aid.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): Another explanation takes it as humbly seeking aid.

positions.position: Al-Kalbi offers an esoteric letter-by-letter gloss: b means beauty, blessing, kindness, and insight; s means radiance, loftiness, and sovereignty; m means glory, dominion, and favor.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (الكلبي): Al-Kalbi offers an esoteric letter-by-letter gloss: b means beauty, blessing, kindness, and insight; s means radiance, loftiness, and sovereignty; m means glory, dominion, and favor.

positions.position: Sulayman ibn Yasar’s letter gloss says b means free of offspring, s hears voices, and m answers prayers.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (سليمان بن يسار): Sulayman ibn Yasar’s letter gloss says b means free of offspring, s hears voices, and m answers prayers.

positions.position: Abu Ruq’s letter gloss says b means creator, s concealer of faults, and m benefactor.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (أبو روق): Abu Ruq’s letter gloss says b means creator, s concealer of faults, and m benefactor.

positions.position: Al-Mawardi says he would omit this letter symbolism if it came from no recognized exegete because it departs from God’s names, but records it without affirming it because an authority transmitted it.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (author): Al-Mawardi says he would omit this letter symbolism if it came from no recognized exegete because it departs from God’s names, but records it without affirming it because an authority transmitted it.

positions.position: The formula may be a declarative statement that the speaker is seeking refuge in God.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): The formula may be a declarative statement that the speaker is seeking refuge in God.

positions.position: Alternatively, its declarative wording functions as a prayer asking the All-Hearing and All-Knowing God to protect the speaker, since He hears prayer and knows how to answer.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): Alternatively, its declarative wording functions as a prayer asking the All-Hearing and All-Knowing God to protect the speaker, since He hears prayer and knows how to answer.

positions.position: From Satan can mean from his whispering.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): From Satan can mean from his whispering.

positions.position: From Satan can alternatively mean from his assistants.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): From Satan can alternatively mean from his assistants.

positions.position: Al-rajim may mean the one who pelts people with calamities and afflictions.
positions.reasons: MAWARDI (unattributed): Al-rajim may mean the one who pelts people with calamities and afflictions.

positions.position: Other derivations connect Allah with seeking refuge in someone, bewilderment (Abū ʿAmr), finding repose with someone (al-Mubarrad), or concealment from lāha.
positions.reasons: JISHUMI (author): Other derivations connect Allah with seeking refuge in someone, bewilderment (Abū ʿAmr), finding repose with someone (al-Mubarrad), or concealment from lāha.

positions.position: Al-Mubarrad links ilāh to Arabic alihtu ilayhi, finding calm with someone; creatures find repose in God and are comforted by remembering Him, as the cited line illustrates.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI (المبرد): Al-Mubarrad links ilāh to Arabic alihtu ilayhi, finding calm with someone; creatures find repose in God and are comforted by remembering Him, as the cited line illustrates.

positions.position: Al-Mubarrad also cites a poetic use of alihtu ilayhi for fleeing or seeking refuge in someone.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI (المبرد): Al-Mubarrad also cites a poetic use of alihtu ilayhi for fleeing or seeking refuge in someone.

positions.position: Al-Mubarrad reads the sequence as bounty upon bounty and favor upon favor.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI (المبرد): Al-Mubarrad reads the sequence as bounty upon bounty and favor upon favor.

positions.position: Other derivations connect the divine name with refuge and bewildered longing: creatures flee to God in hardship and need as a child turns to its mother.
positions.reasons: BAGHAWI-FULL (author): Other derivations connect the divine name with refuge and bewildered longing: creatures flee to God in hardship and need as a child turns to its mother.

positions.position: When a man cursed Satan in the Prophet's presence, the Prophet said this magnified Satan and instructed him to say the basmala, which makes Satan shrink smaller than a fly.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): When a man cursed Satan in the Prophet's presence, the Prophet said this magnified Satan and instructed him to say the basmala, which makes Satan shrink smaller than a fly.

positions.position: The Prophet told a man to invoke the basmala instead of cursing Satan, because it makes Satan shrink to less than a fly.
positions.reasons: IBNATIYYA-FULL (رسول الله): The Prophet told a man to invoke the basmala instead of cursing Satan, because it makes Satan shrink to less than a fly.

positions.position: Another derivation links the name with fleeing for refuge, because creatures turn to God for their needs.
positions.reasons: TABRISI (author): Another derivation links the name with fleeing for refuge, because creatures turn to God for their needs.

positions.position: Al-Mubarrad derives the name from finding repose with God, since creatures become at rest through remembering Him.
positions.reasons: TABRISI (المبرد): Al-Mubarrad derives the name from finding repose with God, since creatures become at rest through remembering Him.

positions.position: Qarḍāb means a cutter, and a sword can be called qarḍāb.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (author): Qarḍāb means a cutter, and a sword can be called qarḍāb.

positions.position: Al-Khaṭṭābī transmits an etymology from a-l-h, meaning to seek refuge; God is so named as the one who protects and grants safety.
positions.reasons: IBNJAWZI-ZAD (أبو سليمان الخطابي): Al-Khaṭṭābī transmits an etymology from a-l-h, meaning to seek refuge; God is so named as the one who protects and grants safety.

positions.position: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.

positions.position: The bāʾ is for attachment and governs an implied verb: “In God’s name I begin performing acts of obedience.”
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): The bāʾ is for attachment and governs an implied verb: “In God’s name I begin performing acts of obedience.”

positions.position: The refuge formula negates improper beliefs and acts, while the basmala affirms what ought to be believed and done; sound reason and clear truth support this order.
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): The refuge formula negates improper beliefs and acts, while the basmala affirms what ought to be believed and done; sound reason and clear truth support this order.

positions.position: Seeking refuge in God means seeking protection from every prohibited act, including sins and wrong beliefs.
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): Seeking refuge in God means seeking protection from every prohibited act, including sins and wrong beliefs.

positions.position: Razi says the roughly seven hundred deviant sects outside the Muslim community add further errors in rational theology and questions of essences and attributes, all covered by seeking refuge.
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): Razi says the roughly seven hundred deviant sects outside the Muslim community add further errors in rational theology and questions of essences and attributes, all covered by seeking refuge.

positions.position: Prohibited actions include whatever the Qur’an, mass-transmitted or solitary reports, communal consensus, or sound analogy forbids; their number exceeds a thousand and the refuge formula encompasses them all.
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): Prohibited actions include whatever the Qur’an, mass-transmitted or solitary reports, communal consensus, or sound analogy forbids; their number exceeds a thousand and the refuge formula encompasses them all.

positions.position: One can seek refuge from something only after knowing it and recognizing its falsehood and ugliness; thus this formula contains thousands of substantial, certain questions.
positions.reasons: RAZI (author): One can seek refuge from something only after knowing it and recognizing its falsehood and ugliness; thus this formula contains thousands of substantial, certain questions.

positions.position: Razi reports the scholarly convention that God has 1,001 sacred names found in scripture and Sunna, and says inquiry into each name is a noble subject.
positions.reasons: RAZI (العلماء): Razi reports the scholarly convention that God has 1,001 sacred names found in scripture and Sunna, and says inquiry into each name is a noble subject.

positions.position: ʿĀʾisha reports finding the Prophet prostrating beside her and supplicating for refuge in God's pleasure, pardon, and self, saying he cannot praise God adequately.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (عائشة): ʿĀʾisha reports finding the Prophet prostrating beside her and supplicating for refuge in God's pleasure, pardon, and self, saying he cannot praise God adequately.

positions.position: Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports from his father the Prophet's instruction not to insult ʿAlī, who was devoted in God's cause.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (كعب بن عجرة): Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra reports from his father the Prophet's instruction not to insult ʿAlī, who was devoted in God's cause.

positions.position: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr reports the Prophet naming Satan's traps: pride in God's blessings, boasting of His gifts, arrogance toward God's servants, and following desire outside God's cause.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (النعمان بن بشير): Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr reports the Prophet naming Satan's traps: pride in God's blessings, boasting of His gifts, arrogance toward God's servants, and following desire outside God's cause.

positions.position: A second etymology derives ilāh from taking refuge or finding rest in someone: minds find rest only in God's remembrance, and souls rise only through knowing Him.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): A second etymology derives ilāh from taking refuge or finding rest in someone: minds find rest only in God's remembrance, and souls rise only through knowing Him. | mentions 13:28

positions.position: Razi connects these arguments to the verse that hearts find rest in remembering God.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Razi connects these arguments to the verse that hearts find rest in remembering God. | mentions 13:28

positions.position: A spiritual master describes purifying the heart like working iron: fear softens it, remembrance cleans it, and persistent renunciation empties it of love besides God until divine love and light fill it.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): A spiritual master describes purifying the heart like working iron: fear softens it, remembrance cleans it, and persistent renunciation empties it of love besides God until divine love and light fill it.

positions.position: Al-ilāh can derive from fleeing in fear and seeking refuge; God alone protects all creatures from harm.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Al-ilāh can derive from fleeing in fear and seeking refuge; God alone protects all creatures from harm. | mentions 23:88

positions.position: As a royal mark protects property from enemies, beginning an act with God’s name marks it against Satan, the enemy of obedience.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): As a royal mark protects property from enemies, beginning an act with God’s name marks it against Satan, the enemy of obedience.

positions.position: Seeking refuge in God signifies rejecting improper beliefs and deeds, while saying in God’s name signifies adopting proper beliefs and deeds; sound reason confirms this order.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Seeking refuge in God signifies rejecting improper beliefs and deeds, while saying in God’s name signifies adopting proper beliefs and deeds; sound reason confirms this order.

positions.position: When the servant remembers God through the opening, God remembers him in turn, as promised in the Qur'an.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): When the servant remembers God through the opening, God remembers him in turn, as promised in the Qur'an. | mentions 2:152

positions.position: Remembrance is a high and honored form of worship: God repeatedly commands abundant remembrance and praises those who remember in every posture and when resisting Satan.
positions.reasons: RAZI-FULL (author): Remembrance is a high and honored form of worship: God repeatedly commands abundant remembrance and praises those who remember in every posture and when resisting Satan. | mentions 2:152, 33:41, 3:191, 7:201

positions.position: Al-Dāraquṭnī transmits Abū Hurayra’s report that 7:204 answered voices raised behind the Prophet; Qurṭubī notes its narrator is weak.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أبو هريرة): Al-Dāraquṭnī transmits Abū Hurayra’s report that 7:204 answered voices raised behind the Prophet; Qurṭubī notes its narrator is weak. | mentions 7:204

positions.position: One view for remembering omitted refuge mid-section is to stop, seek refuge, and restart the section.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أسانيد الحجاز والعراق): One view for remembering omitted refuge mid-section is to stop, seek refuge, and restart the section.

positions.position: A second view is to seek refuge after remembering and resume where reading stopped.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أسانيد الشام ومصر): A second view is to seek refuge after remembering and resume where reading stopped.

positions.position: A report says that when a mount stumbles, saying the basmala makes Satan shrink like a fly, unlike cursing him.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أبو المليح): A report says that when a mount stumbles, saying the basmala makes Satan shrink like a fly, unlike cursing him.

positions.position: Al-Zahrāwī says the verse was revealed concerning prayer; seeking refuge outside prayer is recommended, not obligatory.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (الزهراوي): Al-Zahrāwī says the verse was revealed concerning prayer; seeking refuge outside prayer is recommended, not obligatory.

positions.position: Abū Hurayra and Dāwūd hold that seeking refuge follows recitation.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أبو هريرة وداود): Abū Hurayra and Dāwūd hold that seeking refuge follows recitation.

positions.position: Qurṭubī rejects post-recitation refuge, citing Abū Saʿīd’s report that the Prophet sought refuge before reciting.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Qurṭubī rejects post-recitation refuge, citing Abū Saʿīd’s report that the Prophet sought refuge before reciting.

positions.position: The Prophet teaches a basmala supplication before intimacy, promising protection for a child conceived from Satan’s harm.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): The Prophet teaches a basmala supplication before intimacy, promising protection for a child conceived from Satan’s harm.

positions.position: The Prophet tells ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama to invoke God, eat with the right hand, and take food nearest him; Satan shares food without invocation.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): The Prophet tells ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama to invoke God, eat with the right hand, and take food nearest him; Satan shares food without invocation.

positions.position: For pain, the Prophet tells ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ to say the basmala three times and seek refuge in God’s power seven times.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (عثمان بن أبي العاص): For pain, the Prophet tells ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ to say the basmala three times and seek refuge in God’s power seven times.

positions.position: A report from ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet invoked God when using water for purification, then poured it over his hands.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (عائشة): A report from ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet invoked God when using water for purification, then poured it over his hands.

positions.position: Seeking refuge fulfills the command and protects against Satan’s whispering during recitation.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Seeking refuge fulfills the command and protects against Satan’s whispering during recitation. | mentions 22:52

positions.position: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim reports the Prophet’s opening prayer asking protection from Satan’s hamz, nafkh, and nafth; ʿAmr glosses them as madness, pride, and poetry.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (جبير بن مطعم): Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim reports the Prophet’s opening prayer asking protection from Satan’s hamz, nafkh, and nafth; ʿAmr glosses them as madness, pride, and poetry.

positions.position: Abū Saʿīd reports that the Prophet began night prayer with praise and sought refuge before reciting.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أبو سعيد الخدري): Abū Saʿīd reports that the Prophet began night prayer with praise and sought refuge before reciting.

positions.position: Sulaymān ibn Sālim gives an expanded formula including refuge in God the Mighty and the basmala; Ibn ʿAṭiyya dislikes embellishments without declaring them forbidden.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أبو القاسم): Sulaymān ibn Sālim gives an expanded formula including refuge in God the Mighty and the basmala; Ibn ʿAṭiyya dislikes embellishments without declaring them forbidden.

positions.position: When two men quarreled and one became enraged, the Prophet said seeking refuge from Satan would dispel his anger; Muslim and al-Bukhārī transmit it.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (سليمان بن صرد): When two men quarreled and one became enraged, the Prophet said seeking refuge from Satan would dispel his anger; Muslim and al-Bukhārī transmit it.

positions.position: The Prophet identifies the distracting prayer demon as Khinzab and prescribes seeking refuge and spitting left three times.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي): The Prophet identifies the distracting prayer demon as Khinzab and prescribes seeking refuge and spitting left three times.

positions.position: On a journey at night, the Prophet sought protection from the land’s evils and creatures, including lions, snakes, scorpions, and inhabitants.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (ابن عمر): On a journey at night, the Prophet sought protection from the land’s evils and creatures, including lions, snakes, scorpions, and inhabitants.

positions.position: Istiʿādha means seeking refuge, shelter, or protection from something disliked.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Istiʿādha means seeking refuge, shelter, or protection from something disliked.

positions.position: Shayṭān derives from shaṭana, “to be far,” because Satan is distant from good; the root describes a deep, distant well.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Shayṭān derives from shaṭana, “to be far,” because Satan is distant from good; the root describes a deep, distant well.

positions.position: Most scholars recommend seeking refuge for recitation outside prayer; prayer is disputed.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (الجمهور): Most scholars recommend seeking refuge for recitation outside prayer; prayer is disputed.

positions.position: Some derive shayṭān from burning or perishing, with nūn extra; Sibawayh’s tashayṭana supports derivation from shaṭana instead.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Some derive shayṭān from burning or perishing, with nūn extra; Sibawayh’s tashayṭana supports derivation from shaṭana instead.

positions.position: Rajīm means expelled and disgraced; rajm originally means stoning and can also mean killing, cursing, expulsion, or insult.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Rajīm means expelled and disgraced; rajm originally means stoning and can also mean killing, cursing, expulsion, or insult. | mentions 26:116, 19:46

positions.position: ʿAlī reports seeing the Prophet curse an elephant-shaped figure at al-Ṣafā; it identifies itself as Satan and says it joins the conception of anyone who hates ʿAlī.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (علي بن أبي طالب): ʿAlī reports seeing the Prophet curse an elephant-shaped figure at al-Ṣafā; it identifies itself as Satan and says it joins the conception of anyone who hates ʿAlī.

positions.position: Mujāhid reports that Satan rang four times, including when al-Fātiḥa was revealed, and says it was revealed in Medina.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (مجاهد): Mujāhid reports that Satan rang four times, including when al-Fātiḥa was revealed, and says it was revealed in Medina.

positions.position: Al-Naqqāsh reports that ʿAṭāʾ regards seeking refuge in prayer as obligatory.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (عطاء): Al-Naqqāsh reports that ʿAṭāʾ regards seeking refuge in prayer as obligatory.

positions.position: Ibn Sīrīn and al-Nakhaʿī seek refuge in every prayer unit, applying the command generally.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (ابن سيرين والنخعي): Ibn Sīrīn and al-Nakhaʿī seek refuge in every prayer unit, applying the command generally.

positions.position: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī seek refuge only in the first unit, treating the prayer’s recitation as one reading.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (أبو حنيفة والشافعي): Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī seek refuge only in the first unit, treating the prayer’s recitation as one reading.

positions.position: Mālik does not prescribe refuge in obligatory prayer but does prescribe it in Ramadan night prayer.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (مالك): Mālik does not prescribe refuge in obligatory prayer but does prescribe it in Ramadan night prayer.

positions.position: Scholars agree seeking refuge is not Qurʾān; the majority use the Qurʾānic formula.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (author): Scholars agree seeking refuge is not Qurʾān; the majority use the Qurʾānic formula.

positions.position: Ibn al-Mundhir confirms a brief pause and the Prophet’s supplication asking distance from sins and purification; Abū Hurayra also used it.
positions.reasons: QURTUBI (ابن المنذر): Ibn al-Mundhir confirms a brief pause and the Prophet’s supplication asking distance from sins and purification; Abū Hurayra also used it.

positions.position: Other proposals compare worshippers' clinging in hardship to a calf clinging to its mother, or derive the word from fleeing in fear and receiving refuge.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI (author): Other proposals compare worshippers' clinging in hardship to a calf clinging to its mother, or derive the word from fleeing in fear and receiving refuge.

positions.position: Al-Bayḍāwī calls the metathesis proposal remote and irregular, and derives اسم from elevation because it raises the named thing and marks it.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): Al-Bayḍāwī calls the metathesis proposal remote and irregular, and derives اسم from elevation because it raises the named thing and marks it.

positions.position: الله derives from إله by deleting the hamza and compensating with alif-lām; it is now exclusive to the true deity, though إله originally named any object of worship.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): الله derives from إله by deleting the hamza and compensating with alif-lām; it is now exclusive to the true deity, though إله originally named any object of worship.

positions.position: One etymology derives إله from worship; further proposals connect it with bewilderment, finding rest in God, seeking refuge in fear, or a young animal's attachment to its mother.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): One etymology derives إله from worship; further proposals connect it with bewilderment, finding rest in God, seeking refuge in fear, or a young animal's attachment to its mother.

positions.position: A proposal derives it from وله, “to be bewildered,” with original wāw changing to hamza; the plural آلهة rather than أولهة argues against it.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): A proposal derives it from وله, “to be bewildered,” with original wāw changing to hamza; the plural آلهة rather than أولهة argues against it.

positions.position: The Kufans derive اسم from السمة, originally وسم, with initial wāw deleted and hamzat al-waṣl compensating for it.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (الكوفيون): The Kufans derive اسم from السمة, originally وسم, with initial wāw deleted and hamzat al-waṣl compensating for it.

positions.position: He rejects the Kufan etymology because Arabic does not use an initial hamza this way after deleting a word's first letter.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): He rejects the Kufan etymology because Arabic does not use an initial hamza this way after deleting a word's first letter.

positions.position: If اسم means the spoken expression, it differs from its referent: sounds are discontinuous and vary across peoples and times, whereas the thing named does not.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): If اسم means the spoken expression, it differs from its referent: sounds are discontinuous and vary across peoples and times, whereas the thing named does not.

positions.position: If اسم means the entity itself, it is the referent, but that usage is not well established.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): If اسم means the entity itself, it is the referent, but that usage is not well established.

positions.position: In the commands to bless and glorify God's name, اسم can mean the spoken name, whose wording must be kept free of obscenity and discourtesy just as God and His attributes are free of defects.
positions.reasons: BAYDAWI-FULL (author): In the commands to bless and glorify God's name, اسم can mean the spoken name, whose wording must be kept free of obscenity and discourtesy just as God and His attributes are free of defects. | mentions 55:78, 87:1

positions.position: Asked where the alif of the basmala went, the Messenger replies that Satan stole it; he orders the bāʾ lengthened in its place.
positions.reasons: QASHANI (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): Asked where the alif of the basmala went, the Messenger replies that Satan stole it; he orders the bāʾ lengthened in its place.

positions.position: Unification of acts precedes unification of attributes, which precedes unification of essence; the three are reflected in the Prophet’s prostration supplication seeking refuge in pardon, pleasure, and God Himself.
positions.reasons: QASHANI (author): Unification of acts precedes unification of attributes, which precedes unification of essence; the three are reflected in the Prophet’s prostration supplication seeking refuge in pardon, pleasure, and God Himself.

positions.position: Reported derivations of Allah include roots meaning rising, concealment, refuge or bewilderment, worship, rest, and ecstatic longing; Abū Ḥayyān surveys these competing analyses.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Reported derivations of Allah include roots meaning rising, concealment, refuge or bewilderment, worship, rest, and ecstatic longing; Abū Ḥayyān surveys these competing analyses.

positions.position: Ibn Isḥāq derives Allah from a root meaning to seek refuge, with the hamza omitted.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (ابن إسحاق): Ibn Isḥāq derives Allah from a root meaning to seek refuge, with the hamza omitted.

positions.position: Al-Khalīl and al-Qannād propose derivation from walh, ecstatic longing, with hamza replacing wāw; Abū Ḥayyān calls this weak because the replacement would be obligatory.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (الخليل والقناد): Al-Khalīl and al-Qannād propose derivation from walh, ecstatic longing, with hamza replacing wāw; Abū Ḥayyān calls this weak because the replacement would be obligatory.

positions.position: Abū Ḥayyān omits legal rulings unless the Qur'anic wording itself indicates them or they can be inferred from it; the istiʿādha is not Qur'an by consensus.
positions.reasons: ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Abū Ḥayyān omits legal rulings unless the Qur'anic wording itself indicates them or they can be inferred from it; the istiʿādha is not Qur'an by consensus.

positions.position: A third derivation is alaha, with senses worship, find repose, be bewildered, and fear; the name describes creatures worshipping, seeking refuge, wondering, and fearing God.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): A third derivation is alaha, with senses worship, find repose, be bewildered, and fear; the name describes creatures worshipping, seeking refuge, wondering, and fearing God. | mentions 7:127

positions.position: Ru'ba's word ta'alluh witnesses the worship sense; the verse phrase wa-yadharuka wa-ālihataka is also read as your worship.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (رؤبة): Ru'ba's word ta'alluh witnesses the worship sense; the verse phrase wa-yadharuka wa-ālihataka is also read as your worship. | mentions 7:127

positions.position: A report urging thought about God's blessings, not God Himself, and Ali's saying that reflection on divine attributes ends in bewilderment support the bewilderment sense.
positions.reasons: SAMIN-DURR (author): A report urging thought about God's blessings, not God Himself, and Ali's saying that reflection on divine attributes ends in bewilderment support the bewilderment sense.

positions.position: A report says not to curse Satan after a fall because that makes him swell with pride; saying “in God's name” makes him shrink like a fly (another version says like a house).
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): A report says not to curse Satan after a fall because that makes him swell with pride; saying “in God's name” makes him shrink like a fly (another version says like a house).

positions.position: Because the basmala humbles Satan, it is recommended at the beginning of actions and speech.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR (author): Because the basmala humbles Satan, it is recommended at the beginning of actions and speech.

positions.position: The Prophet taught spouses to say God's name and ask protection from Satan before intercourse; if a child is conceived, Satan will not harm it.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR (رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم): The Prophet taught spouses to say God's name and ask protection from Satan before intercourse; if a child is conceived, Satan will not harm it.

positions.position: Al-Razi lists proposed derivations from bewilderment, repose in God, concealment, a calf's attachment to its mother, and seeking refuge in God.
positions.reasons: IBNKATHIR (فخر الدين الرازي): Al-Razi lists proposed derivations from bewilderment, repose in God, concealment, a calf's attachment to its mother, and seeking refuge in God. | mentions 13:28, 23:88, 16:53, 6:14, 4:78

positions.position: Al-Razi says God alone is the refuge and provider, citing that He protects and cannot be protected against, gives every blessing, feeds without being fed, and all things come from Him.
